topics.title: ראש ממשלת ישראל
topics.description: מסע היסטורי בעקבות מנהיגי מדינת ישראל, מהקמת המדינה ועד לימינו.  גלו את חייהם הייחודיים, הרגעים המכריעים וההשפעה המתמשכת של האישים שהחזיקו בתפקיד הרם ביותר בהנהגת המדינה.  הפעילות מושלמת לכל המשפחה כדי ללמוד יחד על מנהיגות, היסטוריה ואתגרים לאומיים.

categories.title: עובדות חשובות
categories.description: מבט כרונולוגי מלא על כל אדם שכיהן בתפקיד ראש ממשלת ישראל.  קראו יחד את נקודות המבט האישיות וההיסטוריות המרתקות הללו כדי לגלות את הסיפורים הייחודיים  מאחורי כל אחד מהמנהיגים, לפני שתבחנו את הידע שלכם בסבב הטריוויה.

cards.title: דוד בן-גוריון
points: דוד בן-גוריון היה ראש הממשלה הראשון של מדינת ישראל והאיש שהכריז על הקמתה בה' באייר תש"ח.
הוא האמין בכל ליבו בחזון הפרחת השממה ועבר להתגורר בקיבוץ שדה בוקר שבנגב.
בן-גוריון נולד בפולין בשם דוד גרין, ושינה את שמו על שמו של יוסף בן-גוריון, ממנהיגי המרד הגדול בירושלים.
הוא עמד בראש המדינה במהלך מלחמת העצמאות והוביל את גלי העלייה ההמוניים בשנותיה הראשונות של המדינה.

cards.title: משה שרת
points: משה שרת היה ראש הממשלה השני של ישראל, וכיהן בתפקיד במשך תקופה קצרה של כשנתיים בין כהונותיו של בן-גוריון.
הוא היה שר החוץ הראשון של המדינה ונחשב לאדריכל הדיפלומטיה הישראלית ולקו המדיני המתון.
שרת היה בלשן מושבע ששלט באופן שוטף בשש שפות, וטבע מילים רבות בעברית המתחדשת כמו המילה 'אשרור'.
חתימתו מופיעה על מגילת העצמאות, ודיוקנו עיטר בעבר את שטר 20 השקלים של בנק ישראל.

cards.title: לוי אשכול
points: לוי אשכול כיהן כראש הממשלה השלישי והוביל את המדינה לניצחון הצבאי המכריע במלחמת ששת הימים.
הוא הקים את 'מערך המים הארצי' ודחף לביצוע פרויקט מוביל המים הארצי שחיבר את הכנרת לדרום הארץ.
אשכול היה ידוע בחוש הומור ייחודי ובסגנון הנהגה שקול ומפשר שזכה לכינוי 'פוליטיקה של פשרות'.
הוא היה ראש הממשלה הישראלי הראשון שנפטר בעת כהונתו, כתוצאה מהתקף לב בשנת 1969.

cards.title: גולדה מאיר
points: גולדה מאיר הייתה האישה הראשונה והיחידה עד כה שכיהנה כראש ממשלת ישראל, והאישה השלישית בעולם בתפקיד זה.
היא נולדה באוקראינה והגרה בנעוריה לארצות הברית, ולכן דיברה עברית במבטא אמריקאי בולט ומפורסם.
הנהגתה עמדה למבחן הגדול ביותר במהלך מלחמת יום הכיפורים בשנת 1973, משבר שזעזע את המדינה.
המונח 'המטבחון של גולדה' נולד על שם המפגשים הבלתי רשמיים שקיימה עם שרים במטבח ביתה הפרטי.

cards.title: יצחק רבין
points: יצחק רבין היה ראש הממשלה הראשון שנולד בארץ ישראל (יליד ירושלים) והראשון שצמח בפיקוד הצבאי של צה"ל.
הוא כיהן כשתי כהונות נפרדות, ובמהלך כהונתו השנייה חתם על הסכמי אוסלו ועל הסכם השלום עם ירדן.
רבין זכה בפרס נובל לשלום בשנת 1994 יחד עם שמעון פרס ויאסר ערפאת בעקבות מאמצי התהליך המדיני.
חייו נקטעו באופן טרגי ב-4 בנובמבר 1995 כאשר נרצח בתום עצרת שלום בתל אביב על ידי מתנקש יהודי.

cards.title: מנחם בגין
points: מנחם בגין היה ראש הממשלה הראשון מטעם מפלגת הליכוד, וסגר 29 שנות שלטון רצופות של מפלגות הפועלים.
הוא חתם על הסכם השלום ההיסטורי הראשון של ישראל עם מדינה ערבית - הסכם השלום עם מצרים בשנת 1979.
בגין היה נואם מחונן וכריזמטי שזכה לפופולריות עצומה, במיוחד בקרב השכבות העממיות והפריפריה בישראל.
הוא קיבל פרס נובל לשלום יחד עם נשיא מצרים אנואר סאדאת, אך התפטר מתפקידו ב-1983 באמירה המפורסמת 'איני יכול עוד'.

cards.title: יצחק שמיר
points: יצחק שמיר כיהן כראש הממשלה השביעי והיה מפקד לח"י (לוחמי חירות ישראל) ואיש מוסד בכיר בעברו.
הוא נודע בעקשנותו הרבה, באידאולוגיה בלתי מתפשרת של ארץ ישראל השלמה ובסגנון חיים צנוע וספרטני.
במהלך מלחמת המפרץ הראשונה ב-1991, הוביל מדיניות של אי-תגובה למרות מטחי טילי הסקאד העיראקיים כדי לשמור על הקואליציה הבינלאומית.
הוא הוביל את המשלחת הישראלית לוועידת מדריד ההיסטורית, שפתחה לראשונה שיחות ישירות עם מדינות ערב.

cards.title: שמעון פרס
points: שמעון פרס כיהן כראש ממשלה בשתי תקופות שונות, אך מעולם לא ניצח בבחירות ישירות לתפקיד זה.
הוא נחשב לאבי תעשיית הביטחון והטקסטיל בדימונה, וכיהן לאורך חייו כמעט בכל תפקיד ציבורי אפשרי, כולל נשיא המדינה.
הוא הוביל את תוכנית הייצוב הכלכלית של 1985 שהצילה את המשק הישראלי מהיפר-אינפלציה דוהרת.
פרס היה חתן פרס נובל לשלום והקדיש את שנותיו האחרונות לקידום חדשנות טכנולוגית דרך 'מרכז פרס לשלום ולחדשנות'.

cards.title: בנימין נתניהו
points: בנימין נתניהו הוא ראש הממשלה שכיהן את התקופה הארוכה ביותר בתולדות מדינת ישראל, כשהוא עוקף את דוד בן-גוריון.
הוא היה ראש הממשלה הצעיר ביותר שנבחר לתפקיד (בן 46) והראשון שנבחר בשיטת הבחירה הישירה בשנת 1996.
לפני כניסתו לפוליטיקה שירת כקצין בסיירת מטכ"ל ולמד באוניברסיטת MIT היוקרתית בארצות הברית.
בתקופת כהונתו נחתמו 'הסכמי אברהם' ההיסטוריים, שהביאו לנורמליזציה עם איחוד האמירויות, בחריין, מרוקו וסודאן.

cards.title: אהוד ברק
points: אהוד ברק הגיע לפוליטיקה לאחר קריירה צבאית מפוארת, והוא החייל המעוטר ביותר בתולדות צה"ל.
במהלך כהונתו הקצרה כראש ממשלה בשנת 2000, הוביל את הנסיגה המלאה של כוחות צה"ל מרצועת הביטחון בדרום לבנון.
הוא השתתף בוועידת קמפ דייוויד השנייה עם יאסר ערפאת ונשיא ארה"ב ביל קלינטון, בניסיון להגיע להסדר קבע.
ברק מחזיק בתארים מתקדמים בפיזיקה ובמערכות ניתוח מאוניברסיטת סטנפורד היוקרתית.

cards.title: אריאל שרון
points: אריאל שרון, המכונה 'בולדוזר', היה מצביא מפורסם שפיקד על פעולות התגמול והוביל את צליחת תעלת סואץ במלחמת יום הכיפורים.
כראש ממשלה, הוא קיבל את ההחלטה הדרמטית על תוכנית ההתנתקות בשנת 2005, במסגרתה פונו כל היישובים היהודיים מרצועת עזה.
הוא הקים את מפלגת המרכז 'קדימה' לאחר שפרש ממפלגת הליכוד בעקבות התנגדות פנימית לתוכניתו הפוליטית.
כהונתו נקטעה באופן פתאומי בינואר 2006 לאחר שלקה באירוע מוחי חמור ושקע בתרדמת שנמשכה שמונה שנים.

cards.title: אהוד אולמרט
points: אהוד אולמרט מונה לראש הממשלה בפועל לאחר ששרון לקה באירוע מוחי, ובהמשך ניצח בבחירות בראשות מפלגת קדימה.
הוא ניהל את מלחמת לבנון השנייה בשנת 2006 בעקבות חטיפת שני חיילי צה"ל בגבול הצפון.
תחת הנהגתו החשאית, השמיד חיל האוויר הישראלי את הכור הגרעיני הסורי בדיר א-זור בשנת 2007 (מבצע מחוץ לקופסה).
הוא היה ראש הממשלה הישראלי הראשון שנאלץ לרצות עונש מאסר בפועל בעקבות הרשעות בעבירות שחיתות ושחד.

cards.title: נפתלי בנט
points: נפתלי בנט כיהן כראש הממשלה ה-13 של ישראל ועמד בראש 'ממשלת החילופים' הראשונה שכללה מגוון פוליטי רחב במיוחד.
לפני כניסתו לחיים הציבוריים, הוא היה יזם הייטק מצליח שהקים ומכר חברת אבטחת מידע (סאיוטה) בסכום של מיליוני דולרים.
הוא שירת כמפקד צוות בסיירת מטכ"ל וביחידת מגלן, והיה ראש הממשלה הראשון שחבש כיפה סרוגה דרך קבע.
במהלך כהונתו התמודד עם גלי מגפת הקורונה והוביל קו של 'חיים לצד הקורונה' ללא סגרים ארציים.

cards.title: יאיר לפיד
points: יאיר לפיד כיהן כראש הממשלה ה-14 מכוח הסכם החילופים, והוביל את המדינה בתקופת מעבר לקראת בחירות.
לפני פנייתו לפוליטיקה, היה עיתונאי, סופר, ומנחה תוכנית האקטואליה המרכזית והפופולרית ביותר בטלוויזיה בישראל.
במהלך כהונתו הקצרה, פיקד על מבצע 'עלות השחר' ברצועת עזה וחתם על הסכם הגבול הימי ההיסטורי עם לבנון.
הוא מייסד ויו"ר מפלגת 'יש עתיד', אותה הקים בשנת 2012 והפך אותה לכוח מרכזי בפוליטיקה הישראלית.

trivia.question: מי מבין ראשי הממשלה הבאים דיבר עברית במבטא אמריקאי בולט מאחר שהגרה בנעוריה לארה"ב?
איזה ראש ממשלה פתר את בעיית המים של ישראל באמצעות הקמת מפעל מוביל המים הארצי?
מי היה ראש הממשלה הישראלי הראשון שנולד בארץ ישראל עצמה?
איזה ראש ממשלה חתם על הסכם השלום ההיסטורי הראשון עם מצרים בשנת 1979?
מי היה ראש הממשלה היחיד שדיבר הולנדית (דאטש) כשפת אם וגר בעיירה קינדרהוק?
options: השאלה מתייחסת לנשיא ארה"ב מרטין ואן ביורן ולא לראש ממשלה ישראלי

trivia.question: מי היה ראש הממשלה שהנהיג את מדיניות האי-תגובה במהלך מלחמת המפרץ כשטילים נפלו על ישראל?
מי מחזיק בתואר ראש הממשלה שכיהן את התקופה הארוכה ביותר בתולדות המדינה?
איזה ראש ממשלה היה יזם הייטק מצליח והיה לראש הממשלה הראשון שחבש כיפה סרוגה?

categories.title: מלחמות ועימותים
categories.description: מבט מעמיק על האופן שבו מנהיגי המדינה ניהלו משברים צבאיים עצומים, מלחמות קיומיות  והחלטות אסטרטגיות גורליות. למדו כיצד הכרעותיהם בשדה הקרב ובחדרי המצב שינו את פני המזרח התיכון.

cards.title: דוד בן-גוריון
points: הוביל את המדינה הצעירה במהלך מלחמת העצמאות ב-1948 מול פלישת שבעה צבאות ערב.
קיבל את ההחלטה ההיסטורית והמורכבת על פירוק המחתרות (ההגנה, אצ"ל ולח"י) והקמת צה"ל כצבא עם ממלכתי אחד.
יזם וניהל את מלחמת סיני (מבצע קדש) בשנת 1956 בשיתוף פעולה חשאי עם בריטניה וצרפת.
הנהיג את תפיסת הביטחון הישראלית המבוססת על הרתעה, התרעה והכרעה מהירה בשטח האויב.

cards.title: לוי אשכול
points: כיהן כראש הממשלה ושר הביטחון בתקופת ההמתנה המתוחה שלפני מלחמת ששת הימים בשנת 1967.
למרות לחצים כבדים, דחה את היציאה למלחמה עד להבטחת תמיכה דיפלומטית והשלמת מוכנות חיל האוויר.
אישר את מכת המנע המוחצת (מבצע מוקד) שהשמידה את חילות האוויר של מדינות ערב על הקרקע תוך שעות.
תחת הנהגתו איחדה ישראל את ירושלים והרחיבה את שליטתה על יהודה ושומרון, רצועת עזה ורמת הגולן.

cards.title: גולדה מאיר
points: ניהלה את המדינה במהלך מלחמת יום הכיפורים באוקטובר 1973, שנפתחה במתקפת פתע משולבת של מצרים וסוריה.
קיבלה החלטה קשה שלא לצאת למכת מנע מקדימה כדי לא לאבד את התמיכה הדיפלומטית והצבאית של ארצות הברית.
הובילה את המדינה ברגעים האפלים של תחילת הקרבות ועד למהפך הצבאי וכיתור הארמייה השלישית המצרית.
הורתה על הקמת 'ועדת אגרנט' לחקירת המחדל המודיעיני והמבצעי שהוביל לפרוץ המלחמה בהפתעה.

cards.title: מנחם בגין
points: אישר בשנת 1981 את 'מבצע אופרה' - תקיפת חיל האוויר שהשמידה את הכור הגרעיני העיראקי 'אוזירק' שאיים על ישראל.
הוביל את המדינה ליציאה למלחמת לבנון הראשונה (מבצע שלום הגליל) בשנת 1982 במטרה להשמיד את קיני המחבלים.
המלחמה בלבנון הלכה והסתבכה, וגבתה מחיר כבד של אבדות שגרמו לטלטלה ציבורית עמוקה בישראל.
פיתח את 'דוקטרינת בגין' הקובעת כי ישראל לא תאפשר לאף מדינת אויב במזרח התיכון להשיג נשק להשמדה המונית.

cards.title: יצחק רבין
points: פיקד כרמטכ"ל הניצחון על צה"ל במלחמת ששת הימים, מה שהקנה לו מעמד ביטחוני בלתי מעורער בציבור.
במהלך כהונתו הראשונה כראש ממשלה, אישר את 'מבצע יונתן' (מבצע אנטבה) לחילוץ בני הערובה החטופים באוגנדה ב-1976.
כשר ביטחון התמודד עם פרוץ האינתיפאדה הראשונה ב-1987 וגיבש את שיטות העבודה של צה"ל מול לחימה אזרחית.
האמין כי עוצמה צבאית היא הבסיס המאפשר יציאה לתהליכים מדיניים מתוך עמדת כוח מול מדינות ערב.

cards.title: בנימין נתניהו
points: פיקד על שורה ארוכה של מבצעים צבאיים רחבי היקף ברצועת עזה, ביניהם מבצע 'עמוד ענן' ומבצע 'צוק איתן'.
ניהל מערכה חשאית ודיפלומטית רב-שנתית נגד התחמשותה הגרעינית של איראן והתבססותה הצבאית בסוריה.
הוביל את המדינה במהלך מלחמת 'חרבות ברזל' שהחלה בעקבות מתקפת הטרור האכזרית של חמאס בשבעה באוקטובר.
פיתח את אסטרטגיית 'המערכה בין המלחמות' (מב"מ) לסיכול איומים ביטחוניים מחוץ לגבולות המדינה באופן ממוקד.

trivia.question: איזה מבצע צבאי נועז לחילוץ חטופים באוגנדה אושר על ידי יצחק רבין בכהונתו הראשונה?
מי הייתה ראש הממשלה שהובילה את ישראל במהלך ימי מלחמת יום הכיפורים המורכבים?
באיזו מלחמה הוביל לוי אשכול את ישראל לניצחון צבאי מוחץ ותוך כמה ימים היא הסתיימה?
איזה כור גרעיני של מדינת אויב הושמד בהוראתו של מנחם בגין בשנת 1981?

categories.title: מורשת מתמשכת
categories.description: סיור בעקבות המוסדות, חוקי היסוד, ההסכמים הבינלאומיים והתשתיות הלאומיות שקיימים עד היום  בזכות פועלם של מנהיגים אלו. ראו כיצד החלטותיהם עיצבו את דמותה של החברה הישראלית המודרנית.

cards.title: דוד בן-גוריון
points: הניח את היסודות למערכת החינוך הממלכתית וביטל את זרמי החינוך המפלגתיים שהיו נהוגים לפני כן.
נמל התעופה הבינלאומי הראשי של ישראל (נתב"ג) ואוניברסיטת הנגב בבאר שבע קרויים על שמו.
גיבש את הסדר 'סטטוס קוו' בנושאי דת ומדינה, המגדיר את יחסי הממסד הדתי והציבורי בישראל עד היום.
חזונות לביסוס תעשיות המדע והמחקר הוביל להקמת הקריה למחקר גרעיני ומכון ויצמן למדע.

cards.title: מנחם בגין
points: חתם על הסכם קמפ דייוויד שקבע את השלום הרשמי הראשון של ישראל עם הגדולה במדינות ערב - מצרים.
חוקק את חוק יסוד: ירושלים בירת ישראל, המעגן את מעמדה של העיר המאוחדת בחוק הישראלי.
הוביל את מבצע העלייה החשאי הראשון של יהודי אתיופיה (מבצע משה) דרך סודאן בשיתוף המוסד.
הנהיג את פרויקט 'שיקום שכונות' שנועד לצמצם פערים חברתיים וכלכליים בערי הפריפריה.

cards.title: יצחק רבין
points: הוביל לחתימת הסכם השלום ההיסטורי עם ממלכת ירדן בשנת 1994, שפתח את הגבולות והביא לשיתוף פעולה ביטחוני.
הזרים תקציבי עתק חסרי תקדים לפיתוח תשתיות התחבורה, כבישים מהירים ומחלפים שחיברו את הפריפריה למרכז.
חוקק את חוק ביטוח בריאות ממלכתי, שהבטיח שירותי רפואה מתקדמים לכל אזרח ישראלי ללא קשר למצבו הכלכלי.
יום הירצחו נקבע בחוק כיום זיכרון לאומי רשמי (יום הזיכרון ליצחק רבין) לציון חשיבות הדמוקרטיה ומניעת אלימות פוליטית.

cards.title: בנימין נתניהו
points: הוביל את מהפכת השוק החופשי והורדת המכסים, שהפכה את כלכלת ישראל ממרוכזת לתחרותית וגלובלית.
אישר את הקמת גדר הגבול בגבול מצרים, פרויקט שבלם לחלוטין את תופעת ההסתננות הבלתי חוקית מאפריקה.
דחף לפיתוח והפקת הגז הטבעי ממאגרי הים התיכון, מה שהעניק לישראל עצמאות אנרגטית ויתרון כלכלי עצום.
הביא להכרה האמריקאית ההיסטורית בירושלים כבירת ישראל ובהעברת השגרירות האמריקאית אליה.

trivia.question: איזה חוק בריאות חברתי וחשוב חוקק בתקופת ממשלתו של יצחק רבין?
על שמו של איזה מנהיג קרוי נמל התעופה הבינלאומי הראשי של מדינת ישראל?
איזו גדר גבול מאסיבית שנבנתה בתקופת בנימין נתניהו בלמה את ההסתננות הבלתי חוקית לישראל?
איזה הסכם שלום היסטורי נחתם על ידי מנחם בגין בשנת 1979?

topics.title: US Presidents
topics.description: A historic journey through the leaders of the United States, from the founding of the nation to modern times.  Discover the unique lives, crucial moments, and lasting impact of the figures who have held the highest office  in the land. Perfect for the whole family to learn about leadership, history, and the evolution of American democracy.

categories.title: Important Facts
categories.description: A complete chronological look at every single individual who has served as President of the United States.  Read these fascinating, personal, and historic snapshots aloud to discover the unique stories behind all  the commanders-in-chief before testing your knowledge in the trivia round.

cards.title: George Washington
points: George Washington was the only US president to be unanimously elected by the Electoral College.
He is the only president who did not live in Washington, D.C., as it was still being built during his terms.
Contrary to popular myth, his famous false teeth were made of hippopotamus ivory and bone, not wood.
He established the two-term tradition by voluntarily stepping down from power in 1797.

cards.title: John Adams
points: John Adams was the first president to reside in the Executive Mansion, which later became known as the White House.
He was the principal author of the Massachusetts Constitution, which is the world's oldest functioning written constitution.
He died on July 4, 1826, the exact same day as his close friend and political rival Thomas Jefferson.
Adams defended the British soldiers involved in the Boston Massacre in court to ensure a fair trial.

cards.title: Thomas Jefferson
points: Thomas Jefferson was a talented polymath who spoke six languages and invented a specialized wheel cipher for secret codes.
He doubled the size of the United States in 1803 by finalizing the Louisiana Purchase from France.
He kept two grizzly bear cubs in a cage on the White House lawn, which were gifted to him by an explorer.
Jefferson personally designed his famous Virginia home, Monticello, and founded the University of Virginia.

cards.title: James Madison
points: James Madison was the shortest US president in history, standing at 5 feet 4 inches and weighing around 100 pounds.
He is widely hailed as the 'Father of the Constitution' for his pivotal role in drafting the document and the Bill of Rights.
He was one of the three main authors of the Federalist Papers, which argued for the ratification of the Constitution.
During the War of 1812, he became the only sitting president to face active enemy fire on an American battlefield.

cards.title: James Monroe
points: James Monroe's presidency was dubbed the 'Era of Good Feelings' due to a strong sense of national purpose and political unity.
He introduced the Monroe Doctrine, warning European nations that further colonization in the Americas would not be tolerated.
He was the last president of the Revolutionary War generation and the last of the famous Virginia Dynasty.
The capital city of Liberia, Monrovia, was named in his honor due to his support for the colonization society.

cards.title: John Quincy Adams
points: John Quincy Adams was the son of the second president, John Adams, making them the first father-son presidential duo.
He regularly exercised by skinny-dipping in the Potomac River early in the morning during his presidency.
After his presidency, he served in the House of Representatives for 17 years, fighting fiercely against slavery.
He successfully defended the captured African captives of the Amistad ship before the US Supreme Court.

cards.title: Andrew Jackson
points: Andrew Jackson was the first president born in a log cabin and the first to survive an assassination attempt.
He taught his pet parrot how to curse, and the bird reportedly had to be removed from Jackson's funeral for swearing.
He was a notorious duelist who participated in over 100 duels throughout his life to defend his honor.
He completely paid off the national debt in 1835, which is the only time in US history this has occurred.

cards.title: Martin Van Buren
points: Martin Van Buren was the first president born a US citizen, as all previous presidents were originally British subjects.
His native language was Dutch, making him the only US president who spoke English as a second language.
His hometown nickname 'Old Kinderhook' led to the creation of the popular expression 'O.K.' and its universal usage.
He declined to annex Texas during his term to avoid expanding slavery and sparking a war with Mexico.

cards.title: William Henry Harrison
points: William Henry Harrison served the shortest term of any US president, passing away just 32 days after taking office.
He delivered the longest inaugural address in history, speaking for 1 hour and 45 minutes in a freezing storm without a coat.
He was the first president to die while in office, which triggered a brief constitutional crisis over succession.
Before his political career, he gained national fame as a military general at the Battle of Tippecanoe.

cards.title: John Tyler
points: John Tyler was the first vice president to ascend to the presidency due to the death of his predecessor.
He was completely expelled from his own political party, the Whigs, while serving as president due to his policy vetoes.
He fathered 15 children, which is more than any other president in United States history.
He bypassed Congress to officially annex the Republic of Texas into the United States via a joint resolution.

cards.title: James K. Polk
points: James K. Polk was an extremely hardworking leader who achieved every single major campaign goal he set for his single term.
He vastly expanded the nation's borders to the Pacific Ocean by securing the Oregon Territory and winning the Mexican-American War.
He oversaw the opening of the US Naval Academy and the formal establishment of the Smithsonian Institution.
True to his campaign promise to serve only four years, he did not run for reelection and died three months after leaving office.

cards.title: Zachary Taylor
points: Zachary Taylor spent 40 years as a career military officer and rose to fame as a hero of the Mexican-American War.
He had never voted in a presidential election before running for the office himself as the Whig Party nominee.
His beloved warhorse, Old Whitey, lived on the White House lawn and was frequently greeted by tourists.
He died suddenly in office in 1850 after consuming a large quantity of cherries and milk at a July 4th celebration.

cards.title: Millard Fillmore
points: Millard Fillmore was the last member of the Whig Party to ever occupy the White House.
He signed the controversial Compromise of 1850, which temporarily delayed the Civil War but deepened regional divisions.
He and his wife Abigail established the very first permanent library inside the White House.
He sent Commodore Matthew Perry to Japan, successfully opening the isolated island nation to western trade.

cards.title: Franklin Pierce
points: Franklin Pierce was a popular, charming politician who was nicknamed 'Handsome Frank' by his supporters.
He memorized his entire 3,300-word inaugural address and delivered it completely without notes or a script.
He completed the Gadsden Purchase in 1853, buying parts of modern-day Arizona and New Mexico from Mexico.
His presidency was derailed by his support for the Kansas-Nebraska Act, which sparked violent clashes over slavery.

cards.title: James Buchanan
points: James Buchanan remains the only US president in history to never marry, serving his term as a lifelong bachelor.
His niece, Harriet Lane, acted as the official hostess of the White House, coining the term 'First Lady'.
He was a highly experienced diplomat who previously served as Secretary of State and Minister to Great Britain.
His inability to handle the secession crisis allowed the nation to fracture into the Civil War as his term ended.

cards.title: Abraham Lincoln
points: Abraham Lincoln was the tallest US president in history, standing at 6 feet 4 inches without his famous stovepipe hat.
Before entering politics, he was an elite competitive wrestler and is enshrined in the National Wrestling Hall of Fame.
He was the first president born outside of the original thirteen colonies, growing up in a log cabin in Kentucky.
Lincoln was an avid animal lover who allowed his pet cats to eat directly from the White House dinner table.

cards.title: Andrew Johnson
points: Andrew Johnson was a professional tailor before entering politics and famously made his own custom suits as president.
He was the first president to be impeached by the House of Representatives, escaping removal from office by a single Senate vote.
His administration finalized the purchase of Alaska from Russia in 1867, which critics mocked as 'Seward's Folly'.
He did not attend the inauguration of his successor, Ulysses S. Grant, due to intense personal and political bitterness.

cards.title: Ulysses S. Grant
points: Ulysses S. Grant's birth name was Hiram Ulysses Grant, but a clerical error at West Point permanently changed it to U.S. Grant.
He was arrested by a Washington police officer during his presidency for speeding in his horse-drawn carriage.
He established Yellowstone National Park in 1872, creating the world's very first designated national park.
He wrote a critically acclaimed personal memoir while dying of cancer to secure financial stability for his family.

cards.title: Rutherford B. Hayes
points: Rutherford B. Hayes won the most fiercely disputed election in US history, decided by a special congressional commission.
He was the first president to use a telephone in the White House, and his personal phone number was simply the number 1.
He officially banned alcohol and gambling from the White House, earning his wife the nickname 'Lemonade Lucy'.
He voluntarily kept his campaign promise to serve only one term, stepping down from office in 1881.

cards.title: James A. Garfield
points: James A. Garfield was a brilliant mathematician who developed an original geometric proof of the Pythagorean theorem.
He was ambidextrous and could simultaneously write Latin with one hand and Greek with the other.
He was shot by an assassin only four months into his presidency and died 11 weeks later due to unsanitary medical care.
He was the first sitting member of the House of Representatives to be directly elected to the presidency.

cards.title: Chester A. Arthur
points: Chester A. Arthur was a legendary dandy who owned over 80 pairs of pants and changed outfits multiple times a day.
He refused to move into the White House until he redecorated it, auctioning off 24 wagonloads of historic old furniture.
Surprising his critics, he passed the Pendleton Act to eliminate political corruption and create the modern Civil Service system.
He secretly suffered from a fatal kidney ailment throughout his presidency and kept it hidden from the public.

cards.title: Grover Cleveland
points: Grover Cleveland is the only president to serve two non-consecutive terms, counting as both the 22nd and 24th president.
He is the only president who was married inside the White House, wedding Frances Folsom in the Blue Room.
Before entering politics, he worked as a county sheriff and personally performed the duties of a public executioner.
He secretly underwent a successful surgical operation on a yacht to remove a cancerous tumor from his jaw.

cards.title: Benjamin Harrison
points: Benjamin Harrison was the grandson of the 9th president, William Henry Harrison, creating a unique family legacy.
He was the first president to have electricity installed in the White House, but he was too terrified of shocks to touch the switches.
He substantially increased the size of the US Navy and signed the historic Sherman Antitrust Act into law.
During his administration, six new states were admitted to the Union, more than under any other single president.

cards.title: William McKinley
points: William McKinley was the first president to use a telephone for political campaigning and the first to appear on motion picture film.
He wore a red carnation on his lapel at all times as a good luck charm, giving it away to a young girl moments before being shot.
He led the nation to a swift victory in the Spanish-American War, establishing the US as a global power.
His image was placed on the rare $500 bill, which was officially discontinued by the Federal Reserve in 1969.

cards.title: Theodore Roosevelt
points: Theodore Roosevelt was the youngest person to become president, taking office at age 42 after McKinley's assassination.
He was the first American to win a Nobel Peace Prize, awarded for mediating the end of the Russo-Japanese War.
The famous 'Teddy Bear' toy was invented and named in his honor after he refused to shoot a captured bear cub.
He survived an assassination attempt in 1912 and finished his 90-minute speech with a bullet lodged in his chest.

cards.title: William Howard Taft
points: William Howard Taft is the only person in history to serve as both President and Chief Justice of the Supreme Court.
He started the enduring American sports tradition of the president throwing out the ceremonial first pitch at a baseball game.
He was the heaviest president, weighing over 330 pounds, and had a custom, extra-large bathtub installed in the White House.
He completely owned the last presidential cow, Pauline Wayne, who grazed freely on the White House lawn.

cards.title: Woodrow Wilson
points: Woodrow Wilson was a highly accomplished academic and remains the only US president to hold a PhD degree.
He led the nation through World War I and championed the creation of the League of Nations to preserve global peace.
He suffered a debilitating stroke in 1919, after which his wife Edith secretly managed many presidential duties.
He officially designated Mother's Day as a national holiday in 1914 to be celebrated on the second Sunday in May.

cards.title: Warren G. Harding
points: Warren G. Harding was the first president to give a speech over the radio and the first to drive an automobile to his inauguration.
He was an avid poker player who once gambled away an entire set of historic White House china in a single hand.
He hired the first full-time presidential speechwriter to assist him with his public addresses.
He died suddenly of a heart attack in San Francisco during a national speaking tour in 1923.

cards.title: Calvin Coolidge
points: Calvin Coolidge was nicknamed 'Silent Cal' for his famously quiet, stoic personality and concise speaking style.
He kept an extensive exotic pet zoo at the White House, which included a live pygmy hippo named Billy and a raccoon named Rebecca.
He signed the Indian Citizenship Act of 1924, granting full citizenship rights to all Native Americans born in the US.
He is the only US president to have been born on the Fourth of July, arriving in Vermont in 1872.

cards.title: Herbert Hoover
points: Herbert Hoover was a self-made millionaire engineer who spent decades organizing massive global humanitarian food relief programs.
He and his wife Lou Henry spoke fluent Mandarin Chinese in the White House to prevent staff from overhearing private conversations.
He signed the congressional act that officially made 'The Star-Spangled Banner' the national anthem of the United States.
The monumental Hoover Dam on the Colorado River was named in honor of his extensive engineering and political efforts.

cards.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt
points: Franklin D. Roosevelt was the only president elected to four terms, serving through the Great Depression and World War II.
He used the relatively new medium of radio to connect with the public through 30 casual 'Fireside Chats'.
Paralyzed from the waist down by polio in 1921, he went to great lengths to hide his wheelchair use from the public.
He directed the construction of the secret White House underground bunker, which later evolved into the Situation Room.

cards.title: Harry S. Truman
points: Harry S. Truman did not actually have a middle name; his parents gave him the standalone initial 'S' to honor both of his grandfathers.
He made the monumental decision to drop atomic bombs on Japan, effectively ending World War II in August 1945.
He famously kept a sign on his desk that read 'The Buck Stops Here' to show he took full responsibility for all decisions.
His surprising 1848 election victory resulted in a famous, incorrect newspaper headline reading 'Dewey Defeats Truman'.

cards.title: Dwight D. Eisenhower
points: Dwight D. Eisenhower was a five-star general who served as the Supreme Commander of Allied Forces in Europe during World War II.
He authorized the creation of the Interstate Highway System, completely transforming American travel and commerce.
He signed the legislation that created NASA and officially added the phrase 'Under God' to the Pledge of Allegiance.
He was the first president to fly in a helicopter and the first to be barred by law from running for a third term.

cards.title: John F. Kennedy
points: John F. Kennedy was the youngest individual ever elected president, winning the 1960 election at the age of 43.
He was the first Boy Scout to become president and won a Pulitzer Prize for his biographical book 'Profiles in Courage'.
During World War II, his Navy torpedo boat PT-109 was sunk, and he saved his crew by swimming for hours to an island.
He famously launched the Apollo program by declaring the US would land a man on the moon before the 1960s ended.

cards.title: Lyndon B. Johnson
points: Lyndon B. Johnson was sworn in as president aboard Air Force One following the tragic assassination of John F. Kennedy.
He passed the historic Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965 to dismantle legal segregation.
He used an intimidating physical presence and intense persuasion style known as 'The LBJ Treatment' to pass laws.
He created the massive Medicare and Medicaid programs to provide healthcare for elderly and low-income Americans.

cards.title: Richard Nixon
points: Richard Nixon remains the only president in United States history to resign from office, stepping down during the Watergate scandal.
He made a historic trip to communist China in 1972, ending decades of diplomatic isolation between the two nations.
He established the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and signed the Clean Air Act into law.
He spoke directly via telephone to astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin while they were walking on the moon.

cards.title: Gerald Ford
points: Gerald Ford is the only person to serve as both vice president and president without being elected to either office by voters.
He was a star college football player for the University of Michigan and turned down professional offers from the NFL.
He generated intense national controversy by granting a full presidential pardon to Richard Nixon for the Watergate scandal.
He survived two different assassination attempts within a single three-week span in California in 1975.

cards.title: Jimmy Carter
points: Jimmy Carter worked as a successful peanut farmer and a naval nuclear engineer before entering politics.
He successfully mediated the landmark 1978 Camp David Accords, establishing a historic peace treaty between Egypt and Israel.
He lived the longest life of any US president in history, dedicating his decades after office to building homes for charity.
He became the first former president to win the Nobel Peace Prize after leaving the White House for his global diplomacy.

cards.title: Ronald Reagan
points: Ronald Reagan worked as a successful Hollywood actor and appeared in over 50 films before transitioning into politics.
He survived an assassination attempt in 1981, famously joking to his surgeons, 'I hope you are all Republicans.'
To help break his addiction to smoking pipes, Reagan consumed over 300,000 Jelly Belly jelly beans during his presidency.
At age 73, he became the oldest person at the time to be inaugurated for a second presidential term.

cards.title: George H.W. Bush
points: George H.W. Bush was a decorated World War II Navy pilot who survived being shot down over the Pacific Ocean by enemy forces.
He served as the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) and Ambassador to the United Nations before his presidency.
He successfully led a global military coalition to victory in the 1991 Gulf War, liberating the nation of Kuwait.
He signed the landmark Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, protecting millions from discrimination.

cards.title: Bill Clinton
points: Bill Clinton was the first baby boomer president and was famously elected at the young age of 46.
He played the saxophone on national television during his campaign, a move that revolutionized modern political media.
His administration achieved the first federal budget surplus in decades, balancing the national budget for multiple consecutive years.
He became the second president to be impeached by the House, but was ultimately acquitted by the Senate.

cards.title: George W. Bush
points: George W. Bush was the son of the 41st president, making them only the second father-son pair to hold the office.
He led the United States in its response to the September 11 terrorist attacks, establishing the Department of Homeland Security.
Before entering politics, he owned the Texas Rangers professional baseball team and ran an oil exploration company.
He delivered a famous speech via a megaphone at Ground Zero, uniting the country in the days following the 9/11 attacks.

cards.title: Barack Obama
points: Barack Obama was the first African American president of the United States and the first born in Hawaii.
He won a Grammy Award for Best Spoken Word Album for the audio versions of his books before entering the White House.
An avid comic book collector, his favorite characters growing up were Spider-Man and Conan the Barbarian.
He was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2009 for his extraordinary efforts to strengthen international diplomacy.

cards.title: Donald Trump
points: Donald Trump was the first person elected president without any prior political experience or military service.
He built a global real estate empire and hosted the highly successful reality television show 'The Apprentice'.
He established the US Space Force, creating the first completely new branch of the US Armed Forces since 1947.
He appointed three conservative Supreme Court Justices during his single term, reshaping the federal judiciary.

cards.title: Joe Biden
points: Joe Biden served as a US Senator for Delaware for 36 years and as Vice President for 8 years before winning the presidency.
He overcame a severe childhood stutter by practicing reciting poetry alone in front of a mirror for hours.
He was the oldest person to be inaugurated as president, taking the oath of office at the age of 78.
He signed the monumental Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act to upgrade American roads, bridges, and public transit.

trivia.question: Which president spoke English as a second language, having grown up speaking Dutch?
Who was the shortest president in US history, standing at just 5 feet 4 inches?
Which president was an elite wrestler before his political career?
Who is the only person to serve as both US President and Chief Justice of the Supreme Court?
Which president was too terrified of electrical shocks to touch the newly installed light switches?
Which president taught his pet parrot how to curse?
Who was the only president to be unanimously elected by the Electoral College?
Which president survived a shooting in 1912 and still delivered a 90-minute speech with a bullet in his chest?

categories.title: Wars and Conflict
categories.description: A deep dive into how these historical leaders managed massive military crises, international battles,  and defining moments of wartime strategy. Learn how their decisions on the battlefield and in the war room  forever shifted the course of global history.

cards.title: George Washington
points: Before his presidency, Washington served as the Commander-in-Chief of the Continental Army during the American Revolutionary War.
His brilliant surprise crossing of the icy Delaware River on Christmas night 1776 led to a crucial victory at Trenton.
He managed a devastating smallpox outbreak among his troops by ordering an early, secret form of mass inoculation.
He famously resigned his military commission after the war, ensuring civilian control over the newly formed government.

cards.title: Thomas Jefferson
points: Jefferson authorized the First Barbary War in 1801, marking the first time American forces fought on foreign seas and shores.
He refused to pay extortion fees to North African pirates who were actively hijacking American merchant shipping.
He utilized the newly founded US Navy and Marine Corps to successfully blockade enemy ports in the Mediterranean Sea.
The famous lyrics 'to the shores of Tripoli' in the Marine Corps Hymn celebrate the final victory achieved during his term.

cards.title: Abraham Lincoln
points: Lincoln successfully led the United States through the American Civil War, the nation's bloodiest and greatest domestic crisis.
He issued the Emancipation Proclamation in 1863 as a vital military measure, freeing enslaved people in Confederate states.
He cycle-searched through numerous military generals before appointing Ulysses S. Grant to command all Union armies.
His short, powerful Gettysburg Address redefined the war's purpose as a defense of human equality and freedom.

cards.title: Theodore Roosevelt
points: Roosevelt achieved national fame during the Spanish-American War by leading the volunteer cavalry regiment known as the 'Rough Riders'.
He led a legendary, victorious uphill charge during the battle of San Juan Hill in Cuba in 1898.
He is the only US president to receive the Medal of Honor, which was awarded posthumously in 2001 for his wartime bravery.
As president, he modernized the US Navy and sent his 'Great White Fleet' battleships on a peaceful cruise around the world to show American strength.

cards.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt
points: FDR led the United States into World War II following the surprise Japanese military attack on Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941.
He famously termed the Pearl Harbor bombing 'a date which will live in infamy' during his historic address to Congress.
He worked closely with Allied leaders Winston Churchill and Joseph Stalin to orchestrate the global strategy against the Axis powers.
He secretly authorized the Manhattan Project, the top-secret scientific program that successfully developed the first atomic weapons.

cards.title: John F. Kennedy
points: Kennedy navigated the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis, widely considered the closest the world has ever come to an all-out nuclear war.
Instead of launching an immediate airstrike, he ordered a strategic naval 'quarantine' or blockade around the island of Cuba.
He established a direct telephone 'hotline' between Washington and Moscow to prevent accidental military escalations in the future.
He authorized the ill-fated Bay of Pigs invasion in 1961, an unsuccessful secret attempt to overthrow the Cuban government.

cards.title: Ronald Reagan
points: Reagan implemented a grand strategy to escalate the Cold War, aggressively increasing US military spending to pressure the Soviet Union.
He famously labeled the Soviet Union as an 'evil empire' during a high-profile public speech in 1983.
He championed the Strategic Defense Initiative, a space-based anti-missile shield project nicknamed 'Star Wars' by the media.
In 1987, he delivered a speech at the Berlin Wall, directly challenging Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev to 'tear down this wall!'

cards.title: Barack Obama
points: Obama authorized the highly secret 2011 Navy SEAL raid in Pakistan that resulted in the death of terrorist leader Osama bin Laden.
He significantly expanded the strategic use of unmanned aerial drone strikes against militant targets in the Middle East.
He successfully fulfilled a campaign promise by drawing down and ending major US combat operations in the Iraq War.
He ordered a massive surge of 30,000 additional US troops into Afghanistan to combat rising Taliban insurgencies.

categories.title: Lasting Legacy
categories.description: An exploration of the enduring monuments, political institutions, systemic laws, and physical landscapes  that remain today because of these leaders. See how their actions molded the physical and cultural map of  modern America.

cards.title: George Washington
points: Washington's likeness is immortalized in stone on Mount Rushmore and features prominently on both the US quarter and the one-dollar bill.
The nation's capital city, an entire state, 31 counties, and dozens of universities are directly named in his honor.
He established the traditional cabinet system, appointing original heads of departments to advise the chief executive.
His farewell address set a lasting precedent warning America against permanent foreign alliances and political parties.

cards.title: Thomas Jefferson
points: Jefferson authored the Declaration of Independence, framing the founding ideals of American freedom and human rights.
His massive personal library of over 6,000 books was sold to the government to rebuild the Library of Congress after a fire.
He is sculpted on Mount Rushmore and his image has been featured on the US nickel coin since 1938.
His collection of historic artifacts from the Lewis and Clark expedition helped establish early American natural sciences.

cards.title: Abraham Lincoln
points: Lincoln is commemorated at the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C., the historic site of many famous civil rights speeches.
He signed the 1862 Homestead Act, which allowed millions of citizens to claim free land in the American West.
He officially established Thanksgiving as a national annual holiday in 1863 to help unite a fractured country.
His face is depicted on the US penny and the five-dollar bill, as well as carved into South Dakota's Mount Rushmore.

cards.title: Theodore Roosevelt
points: Roosevelt created the United States Forest Service and signed the Antiquities Act to protect massive tracts of wilderness.
He established 150 national forests, 51 federal bird reserves, and 5 national parks, protecting roughly 230 million acres.
He fiercely broke up corporate monopolies, earning the enduring historical nickname of the 'Trust Buster'.
His monumental impact on American development earned him a place alongside Washington, Jefferson, and Lincoln on Mount Rushmore.

cards.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt
points: FDR established the Social Security system in 1935, creating a lasting financial safety net for retired American workers.
He created the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to monitor the stock market and protect everyday investors.
His New Deal programs built thousands of American roads, bridges, public schools, and massive dams that are still used today.
His legacy is honored on the US dime coin, recognizing his work founding the March of Dimes organization to combat polio.

cards.title: John F. Kennedy
points: Kennedy established the Peace Corps in 1961, sending thousands of American volunteers abroad to assist developing nations.
The nation's primary space center in Florida, Cape Canaveral, was renamed the Kennedy Space Center shortly after his death.
He proposed the sweeping civil rights legislation that eventually became the historic Civil Rights Act of 1964.
An eternal flame burns continuously at his gravesite in Arlington National Cemetery, visited by millions every year.

cards.title: Ronald Reagan
points: Reagan popularized supply-side economics, a policy framework heavily centered on deregulation and tax cuts known as 'Reaganomics'.
He appointed Sandra Day O'Connor in 1981, making her the first woman to ever serve on the Supreme Court.
Washington National Airport was officially renamed Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in his honor in 1998.
His political style permanently shifted the modern Republican Party toward a philosophy of limited government intervention.

cards.title: Barack Obama
points: Obama signed the landmark 2010 Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act, universally known as 'Obamacare'.
He nominated Sonia Sotomayor, who became the first Hispanic Justice to serve on the US Supreme Court.
He signed the historic Obergefell v. Hodges brief supporting the federal legalization of same-sex marriage nationwide.
He authorized the dynamic American Recovery and Reinvestment Act to successfully reboot the economy after the 2008 financial crisis.

topics.title: US States
topics.description: Facts and trivia about the United States, ordered from the largest state by land area to the smallest.

categories.title: Important Facts
categories.description: Interesting facts about each US state, ordered by land area.

cards.title: Alaska
points: Alaska is the largest US state, covering more than 663,000 square miles.
It was purchased from Russia in 1867 and became a state in 1959.
Denali, North America's tallest mountain, is located in Alaska.
Alaska has more coastline than all the other US states combined.
Juneau is the only US state capital that cannot be reached by road.

cards.title: Texas
points: Texas is the second-largest state in both land area and population.
It was an independent republic from 1836 until joining the United States in 1845.
Houston is home to NASA's Johnson Space Center.
The Alamo in San Antonio is one of America's most famous historic sites.
Texas produces more wind power than any other US state.

cards.title: California
points: California is the most populous US state.
Silicon Valley is a global center for technology and innovation.
Hollywood is the world's best-known film production district.
Death Valley contains the lowest point in North America.
Mount Whitney is the tallest mountain in the contiguous United States.

cards.title: Montana
points: Montana is known as Big Sky Country.
Glacier National Park contains hundreds of lakes and glaciers.
Part of Yellowstone National Park extends into Montana.
Montana has one of the lowest population densities in the United States.
The state is home to abundant wildlife including grizzly bears and bison.

cards.title: New Mexico
points: Santa Fe is the oldest state capital in the United States.
White Sands National Park features brilliant white gypsum dunes.
The state has strong Native American and Hispanic cultural influences.
Los Alamos played a key role in the Manhattan Project.
New Mexico is nicknamed the Land of Enchantment.

cards.title: Arizona
points: Grand Canyon National Park attracts millions of visitors every year.
Arizona became the 48th state in 1912.
The Sonoran Desert is home to the giant saguaro cactus.
Meteor Crater is one of the world's best-preserved impact craters.
Phoenix is one of the fastest-growing major cities in the United States.

cards.title: Nevada
points: Las Vegas is one of the world's most famous entertainment cities.
Most of Nevada is covered by desert landscapes.
Lake Tahoe sits on the California-Nevada border.
Nevada is known as the Silver State because of its mining history.
Area 51, a highly secretive military site, is located in southern Nevada.

cards.title: Colorado
points: Colorado has the highest average elevation of any US state.
The Rocky Mountains dominate much of the state's landscape.
Denver is known as the Mile High City because its elevation is about one mile above sea level.
Pikes Peak inspired the song 'America the Beautiful.'
Colorado has four national parks.

cards.title: Oregon
points: Crater Lake is the deepest lake in the United States.
The Oregon Trail ended in the fertile Willamette Valley.
The state has no statewide sales tax.
Oregon's Pacific coastline is entirely public land.
Portland is famous for bicycles, bridges, and coffee culture.

cards.title: Wyoming
points: Yellowstone became the world's first national park in 1872.
Devils Tower was America's first National Monument.
Wyoming was the first state to grant women the right to vote.
Grand Teton National Park contains some of North America's most dramatic mountains.
Wyoming has the smallest population of any US state.

cards.title: Michigan
points: Michigan is made up of two peninsulas connected by the Mackinac Bridge.
It borders four of the five Great Lakes.
Detroit became the birthplace of the modern automobile industry.
Michigan has the longest freshwater coastline in the United States.
The state has more than 11,000 inland lakes.

cards.title: Minnesota
points: Minnesota is known as the Land of 10,000 Lakes.
The Mississippi River begins at Lake Itasca.
The Twin Cities are Minneapolis and Saint Paul.
The Mall of America is one of the largest shopping malls in the country.
Minnesota experiences some of the coldest winters in the continental United States.

cards.title: Utah
points: Utah is home to the Mighty Five national parks.
Arches National Park contains more than 2,000 natural stone arches.
The Great Salt Lake is the largest saltwater lake in the Western Hemisphere.
Salt Lake City hosted the 2002 Winter Olympics.
Utah's red rock landscapes are famous around the world.

cards.title: Idaho
points: Idaho produces more potatoes than any other US state.
Hells Canyon is deeper than the Grand Canyon.
More than half of Idaho is public land.
Boise is the state's capital and largest city.
The state offers excellent opportunities for hiking, skiing, and rafting.

cards.title: Kansas
points: Kansas is known as the Sunflower State.
The state is one of the nation's largest wheat producers.
Kansas lies near the geographic center of the contiguous United States.
The story of 'The Wizard of Oz' begins in Kansas.
The Flint Hills preserve one of the world's largest remaining tallgrass prairies.

cards.title: Nebraska
points: Nebraska has the only single-house state legislature in the United States.
The state is a leading producer of corn and beef.
Chimney Rock guided pioneers traveling west.
Sandhill cranes gather in huge numbers along the Platte River each spring.
Lincoln is the capital while Omaha is the largest city.

cards.title: South Dakota
points: Mount Rushmore National Memorial features the faces of four US presidents.
Badlands National Park contains colorful rock formations and fossils.
The Crazy Horse Memorial is one of the world's largest mountain carvings.
The Black Hills are sacred to many Native American tribes.
South Dakota is famous for its annual Sturgis Motorcycle Rally.

cards.title: Washington
points: Washington is the nation's leading producer of apples.
Seattle is home to major technology companies and the Space Needle.
Mount Rainier is an active volcano rising more than 14,000 feet.
Olympic National Park contains mountains, rainforest, and Pacific coastline.
The state borders Canada and the Pacific Ocean.

cards.title: North Dakota
points: Theodore Roosevelt National Park protects colorful badlands and bison.
North Dakota is a leading producer of wheat, sunflowers, and canola.
The Bakken oil fields have made the state a major energy producer.
Bismarck is the state capital.
North Dakota became a state in 1889.

cards.title: Oklahoma
points: Oklahoma has one of the largest Native American populations in the United States.
Route 66 crosses more miles in Oklahoma than in any other state.
The Land Run of 1889 helped settle much of the territory.
Oklahoma experiences some of the world's most frequent tornadoes.
The state capital is Oklahoma City.

cards.title: Missouri
points: The Gateway Arch in St. Louis is the tallest monument in the United States.
The Missouri and Mississippi Rivers meet near St. Louis.
Mark Twain grew up in Hannibal.
Branson is famous for live entertainment.
Missouri is known as the Show-Me State.

cards.title: Florida
points: Florida has the longest coastline in the contiguous United States.
Everglades National Park protects a unique subtropical ecosystem.
The Kennedy Space Center is where many NASA missions have launched.
Florida is one of the world's most popular tourist destinations.
The state is the nation's largest producer of oranges.

cards.title: Wisconsin
points: Wisconsin is America's leading cheese-producing state.
The Green Bay Packers are one of the NFL's oldest franchises.
Milwaukee has a long brewing tradition.
The state borders Lakes Michigan and Superior.
Door County is famous for cherries and scenic shoreline.

cards.title: Georgia
points: Atlanta is one of the largest cities in the southeastern United States.
Georgia is nicknamed the Peach State.
Martin Luther King Jr. was born in Atlanta.
Savannah is famous for its historic squares.
The world's busiest airport is located in Atlanta.

cards.title: Illinois
points: Chicago is the third-largest city in the United States.
The Willis Tower was once the world's tallest building.
Route 66 begins in downtown Chicago.
Illinois is known as the Land of Lincoln.
The first McDonald's franchise opened in Des Plaines.

cards.title: Iowa
points: Iowa is one of America's leading corn-producing states.
The Iowa State Fair is one of the country's largest agricultural fairs.
The Iowa caucuses traditionally begin the presidential election season.
Des Moines is the capital and largest city.
The state's fertile farmland is part of the Corn Belt.

cards.title: New York
points: New York City is the largest city in the United States.
The Statue of Liberty welcomed millions of immigrants.
Niagara Falls is one of North America's most famous waterfalls.
The Adirondack Park is larger than Yellowstone, Yosemite, Glacier, Grand Canyon, and Great Smoky Mountains National Parks combined.
Albany is the state capital.

cards.title: North Carolina
points: The Wright brothers made the first successful powered flight at Kitty Hawk.
Research Triangle Park is a major center for science and technology.
The Great Smoky Mountains extend into western North Carolina.
North Carolina produces more sweet potatoes than any other state.
The Cape Hatteras Lighthouse is America's tallest brick lighthouse.

cards.title: Arkansas
points: Crater of Diamonds State Park lets visitors keep any diamonds they find.
Hot Springs National Park protects natural thermal springs.
Arkansas is nicknamed the Natural State.
The Buffalo National River was America's first national river.
Little Rock is the state capital.

cards.title: Alabama
points: The first 911 emergency call was made in Haleyville in 1968.
NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville helped develop the Saturn V rocket.
Montgomery was the first capital of the Confederate States.
Alabama is known as the Yellowhammer State.
The USS Alabama battleship is now a museum.

cards.title: Louisiana
points: New Orleans is famous for Mardi Gras celebrations.
Jazz music was born in New Orleans.
Louisiana is the only state divided into parishes instead of counties.
The state has extensive wetlands known as bayous.
The Mississippi River has shaped Louisiana's history and economy.

cards.title: Mississippi
points: The Mississippi River forms the state's western border.
The state is considered the birthplace of the blues.
Jackson is the capital and largest city.
Magnolia is the state flower.
Mississippi became the 20th state in 1817.

cards.title: Pennsylvania
points: The Declaration of Independence was signed in Philadelphia.
The Liberty Bell is one of America's best-known symbols.
The Battle of Gettysburg was a turning point in the Civil War.
Hershey is known as the Chocolate Capital of the United States.
Pennsylvania was one of the original thirteen colonies.

cards.title: Ohio
points: Ohio is known as the Buckeye State.
The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame is located in Cleveland.
Several US presidents were born in Ohio.
The Wright brothers were from Dayton.
Cedar Point is one of the world's most famous amusement parks.

cards.title: Virginia
points: Jamestown was the first permanent English settlement in North America.
Virginia is known as the birthplace of eight US presidents.
Shenandoah National Park protects part of the Blue Ridge Mountains.
Arlington National Cemetery is located in Virginia.
The state played a major role in the American Revolution and Civil War.

cards.title: Tennessee
points: Nashville is known as Music City because of its country music industry.
Memphis is famous for blues music and the birthplace of rock and roll.
Great Smoky Mountains National Park is the most visited national park in the United States.
The Grand Ole Opry has been broadcasting from Nashville for decades.
The state is known for whiskey production.

cards.title: Kentucky
points: The Kentucky Derby is one of the world's most famous horse races.
Mammoth Cave is the longest known cave system in the world.
Kentucky is famous for bourbon production.
The state is known for thoroughbred horse farms.
Frankfort is the state capital.

cards.title: Indiana
points: The Indianapolis 500 is one of the world's most famous auto races.
Indiana is known as the Hoosier State.
The state has a strong basketball tradition.
The first professional baseball game was played in Fort Wayne.
Indianapolis is both the state capital and largest city.

cards.title: Maine
points: Maine is the easternmost state in the United States.
The state is famous for lobster fishing.
Acadia National Park protects mountains, forests, and coastline.
Maine has the largest forest area of any New England state.
Augusta is the state capital.

cards.title: South Carolina
points: Fort Sumter was where the first shots of the Civil War were fired.
Charleston is famous for its historic architecture and harbor.
Myrtle Beach is one of the state's most popular vacation destinations.
The state is nicknamed the Palmetto State.
South Carolina was the first state to secede from the Union in 1860.

cards.title: West Virginia
points: West Virginia became a separate state during the Civil War in 1863.
The New River Gorge is famous for outdoor adventures.
The state is known as the Mountain State.
Charleston is the capital.
Coal mining has played an important role in the state's history.

cards.title: Maryland
points: Maryland surrounds much of the Chesapeake Bay.
The state is famous for blue crabs.
The US Naval Academy is located in Annapolis.
Baltimore is known for its Inner Harbor.
Maryland is nicknamed America in Miniature because of its varied landscapes.

cards.title: Hawaii
points: Hawaii is the only US state made entirely of islands.
It became the 50th state in 1959.
Mauna Kea is taller than Mount Everest when measured from its ocean base.
Hawaii Volcanoes National Park contains active volcanoes.
The state is the only place in the United States where coffee is commercially grown.

cards.title: Massachusetts
points: The Pilgrims arrived at Plymouth in 1620.
Boston played a major role in the American Revolution.
Harvard University is the oldest university in the United States.
The Boston Tea Party helped spark the American Revolution.
Cape Cod is a famous coastal vacation area.

cards.title: Vermont
points: Vermont is famous for maple syrup production.
The Green Mountains give the state its name.
Vermont was once an independent republic.
Montpelier is the smallest US state capital by population.
The state is known for farms, forests, and outdoor recreation.

cards.title: New Hampshire
points: New Hampshire's motto is 'Live Free or Die.'
Mount Washington is famous for extreme weather conditions.
The state was one of the original thirteen colonies.
New Hampshire holds the first presidential primary in many election cycles.
The White Mountains attract hikers and visitors.

cards.title: New Jersey
points: New Jersey is one of the most densely populated US states.
Thomas Edison developed many inventions in New Jersey.
Atlantic City is famous for its boardwalk.
Princeton University is located in the state.
The state shares the Statue of Liberty with New York.

cards.title: Connecticut
points: Connecticut was one of the original thirteen colonies.
Yale University is located in New Haven.
The state is known as the Constitution State.
The first hamburger is often credited to a restaurant in New Haven.
Mystic Seaport preserves America's maritime history.

cards.title: Delaware
points: Delaware was the first state to ratify the US Constitution.
It is the second-smallest state by area.
The state has no sales tax.
Dover is the capital.
Delaware is known as the First State.

cards.title: Rhode Island
points: Rhode Island is the smallest US state by area.
It was one of the original thirteen colonies.
Newport is famous for historic mansions and sailing.
Providence is the state capital.
The state has a long Atlantic Ocean coastline.
